markets.cadence: daily, published same evening after close via KRX/press

flows.note: Net sold as KOSPI touched an intraday record 7,153 before paring gains into the 4-day Chuseok closure (24-27 Sep)
Lone net buyer of the session, lifting KOSPI to a fresh closing record despite foreign and retail selling
Heavy pre-holiday profit-taking ahead of the 4-day Chuseok market closure

markets.trend: KOSPI closed at a fresh record 7,080.92 (+63.01pt, +0.90%) on 23 Sep, the third straight record-setting session, after spiking to an intraday high of 7,153 on NY-led AI/semiconductor strength; gains were pared into the close as position-adjustment ahead of the 4-day Chuseok holiday (24-27 Sep) took hold. Institutions were the only net buyer (+₩317.0bn) while both foreigners (-₩510.1bn) and retail (-₩1,439.7bn, the largest single-day retail outflow of the recent run) sold, a reversal of the smaller, rotating flows seen on 21-22 Sep.
markets.interpretation: A third consecutive record close on institution-only buying, with both foreign and retail investors de-risking ahead of a 4-day market closure, reads as pre-holiday position trimming rather than a change in trend -- but the size of the retail and foreign outflows (the largest of the week) leaves the reopening session (29 Sep, after Chuseok) as a key tell for whether North Asia tech conviction (relevant to the owner's exposure) survives the break or whether profit-taking resumes.
dataGaps: KRX daily investor-type data does not separately break out retail vs. proprietary/pension components within 'institutions'
Korean markets are closed 24-27 Sep for Chuseok; no new daily print will be available until the 29 Sep reopen

markets.trend: Southbound net buying extended to a 13th consecutive session on 23 Sep but slowed sharply to +HK$3.449bn, roughly a quarter of 22 Sep's pace (+HK$12.691bn). Top net buys were Tencent (+HK$2.035bn) and Xiaomi-W (+HK$0.457bn); top net sells were Kingboard Laminates (-HK$2.168bn, a reversal from being a net buy on 22 Sep), Zhipu AI (-HK$0.3bn, also reversing from 22 Sep's top buy) and SMIC (-HK$0.331bn).
markets.interpretation: The streak's 13th day but at a much slower pace, with the prior session's AI/optical darlings (Zhipu, Kingboard Laminates) flipping to net sells while flows rotate back into Tencent, suggests mainland conviction into HK is cooling from its recent one-month-high pace even though it remains net positive -- a mild caution signal for the owner's HK tech book (0700/0981/1810) after twelve days of accelerating support, worth watching for whether the deceleration continues or reverses once Korea reopens post-Chuseok.
